waivers.reason: The interim bridge's database stamps rows with its own clock, so no permitted written_time_source can be declared, and its FACTS time_governance does not cover the plant MQTT brokers it reads. Waived with admin privileges until the bridge is fixed or replaced.
The interim bridge owns its PostgreSQL database and holds its own credential until the data moves into the hub's mod_mes schema.
The interim bridge ships its own Next.js frontend as the MES user interface until forge-display exists.
No module ships a roles file yet: the roles file has no FxTS spec to be written against, and the hub still uses its own flat roles.
The interim bridge is the imported NestJS application, not built from the module SDK; the Go forge-mes replaces it.
The record id rule of the transport contract (T-5) is not built: records carry an id the adapter makes, and the hub does not yet keep each id once.
Store and forward is not part of the module SDK yet (T-6): the module does not buffer what it cannot deliver.
The goodbye and the last will of the transport contract (T-8) are not built: the hub learns of a shutdown only when calls stop.
The once-and-only-once rule for business write-backs is not built: a write-back carries no id for the module to apply once and confirm.

metadata.hosting: interim: NestJS backend and Next.js frontend under forge-modules/forge-mes/bridge, with the hub-side spoke under src/forge/adapters/forge_mes
metadata.note: M-3 is a time-keeping requirement: its waiver counts only once the owner approves this spec (Q-10). The bridge's Redis cache and RabbitMQ broker were not assessed (FB-145). No FVTS spec describes the MES screens; M-9 is waived.
